label: original-phase z/f input following a z/b/f/q/e/u/3/w/0 token (bigram detector)
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t >= 1) & ((isin(in_tok, [tok("z"), tok("f")]) & isin(prev_tok, [tok("z"),tok("b"),tok("f"),tok("q"),tok("e"),tok("u"),tok("3"),tok("w"),tok("0")])) | ((prev_tok == tok("z")) & isin(in_tok, [tok("c"), tok("e"), tok("3"), tok("d")])))
explanation: Fires almost only in the original-input phase (95% of mass), never at t=0, peaking at t=1-3 and falling off with position. Behaves like an additive current-token + previous-token detector: current input z or f carries most mass (z 40%, f 31%; c, e, 3 weaker), boosted when the previous input is z (strongest), b, f, q, e, u, 3, w or 0. The largest activations are z right after z at step 2 (e.g. z z z ..., b z z ...). Rarely fires in the copy phase or at the delimiter. Plain z/f input is too broad (precision about 0.2); requiring a boosting previous token gives dev F1 about 0.51 and mass recall about 0.66. The leftover is spread across many weak token pairs, so no simple predicate is precise.
